reason: Prompt caching is the intended optimization for a large static repeated prefix, cutting input cost and TTFT with no model/quality change. PT, batch (async), and fine-tuning are all wrong for an interactive low-latency chatbot.

Bedrock fine-tuned/custom models cannot be served on-demand; Provisioned Throughput (model units) is required. Quota increase, cross-Region, and a training flag cannot create an on-demand path for a private custom model.
Latency-optimized inference runs supported models on infrastructure tuned for lower latency, directly targeting the SLA. Batch and SQS add delay; max_tokens is only an output cap.

Model distillation transfers teacher behavior to a smaller cheaper student, ideal for a narrow high-volume task with labeled data. PT on the large model keeps high per-token cost; batch is async; temperature does not control cost.

A cross-Region inference profile spreads on-demand requests across Regions, raising effective throughput and resilience with minimal re-architecture. No-backoff retries worsen throttling; PT at average rate still throttles at spikes; batch abandons real-time.

AWS Budgets gives proactive actual/forecast cost alerts; CloudWatch Bedrock metrics (InputTokenCount, OutputTokenCount, Invocations) track token usage. Shield (DDoS), Guardrails (content), and Free Tier dashboard do not control or attribute spend.

Sustained high, predictable 24/7 utilization is exactly where Provisioned Throughput with a term commitment beats on-demand. Cross-Region does not cut per-token price; batch cannot serve continuous real-time; top_p does not affect cost.

With cost driven by redundant input tokens, reranking plus tighter top-k keeps only relevant chunks, shrinking input tokens while preserving quality. max_tokens is output-side; PT does not discount oversized prompts; temperature does not change what context is sent.
